title: Give a Function the Full Situation
content:
What problem does this solve?
A function can make a decision only if it knows the whole situation. Multiple **parameters** let the caller describe everything the function needs — not rely on global names.

Basic syntax
  def label(destination, status):
      return f"{destination}: {status}"
  print(label("Gloamfen", "Review"))

What actually happens
- Arguments bind to parameters **by position** unless you use keywords
- A function can receive lists or dictionaries as parameters

When this is useful
Describe the whole decision at the call site; make functions reusable and testable.
concepts: Parameters bind by position unless keywords are used
Functions can receive lists and dicts as inputs
Order matters when calling without keywords

examples.title: Two inputs bind in order
examples.explanation: The first argument binds to destination; the second to status.

common_mistakes: Swapping the order of arguments at the call site
Relying on *args instead of naming the parameters

exercises.title: Two inputs bind in order
hints: The first argument is the destination.
Think f-strings: destination colon space status.

exercises.title: Name both parameters
exercises.prompt: Complete the function signature with two named parameters.
hints: Declare two parameters named price and quantity.

exercises.title: Swapped at the call site
exercises.prompt: Fix the call so name appears before role.
hints: Arguments bind left to right when called by position.
Swap the two string arguments in the print.

exercises.title: Carry capacity
exercises.prompt: Write carry_capacity(base_slots, bonus_slots) that returns their sum.
hints: Add the two parameters and return the result.
The sum can be written base_slots + bonus_slots.
Handle zero and negative adjustments — behavior decides.

exercises.title: Dispatch status
exercises.prompt:
Write dispatch_status(party, supplies, warning_active):

- Return "Denied" when warning_active is True or party is empty
- Otherwise return "Ready" when supplies has at least two items per party member
- Otherwise return "Review"

Require exactly the named three-parameter signature.
hints: First, deny if warning_active or party is empty.
Compare counts with len(supplies) and len(party).
Return Ready only if supplies >= 2 * len(party).

tests.message: Use len(...) for counts in dispatch_status.

exercises.success_message: I can design a function whose parameters describe the whole decision.
